text:
Maya: Quick question — how should we map quota tiers to pricing plans for per-key vs per-org enforcement? Planning console UX + routing policies.
Ravi: My instinct: default per-key for free/pro, per-org for enterprise. Keeps simple for self-serve.
Jess: Agreed, but we need a clear fallback when an org buys Dedicated capacity — should per-key limits still apply?
Tom: If Dedicated is reserved capacity, routing should bypass per-key soft-limits and use org pool. So enforcement mode changes at routing time.
Maya: That implies we need a runtime switch: `enforcement_mode: per_key | per_org | pool` and a deterministic precedence rule.
Ravi: Proposal: resolution order = explicit org override -> dedicated pool binding -> plan default. If org override exists, always honor.
Jess: UX note: Console should surface which mode is active and why (e.g., "Bound to Dedicated pool: org override"). Users keep confused otherwise.
Maya: Telemetry question: what labels do we add so billing/console can show accurate charts?
Arthur: Add `quota_mode`, `quota_source` (plan|org|pool), and `burst_bucket_id`. That covers attribution.
QuotaBot: Reminder: existing meter expects `key_id` and `org_id`. New labels will be optional but recommended.
Tom: Burst handling detail: free/pro get small per-key burst buckets; enterprise can opt into shared org burst pool. Need leak/bucket semantics.
Ravi: Implementation sketch:
```
# mapping config
plans:
  free:
    enforcement: per_key
    burst: { type: per_key, tokens: 500, window_s: 60 }
  pro:
    enforcement: per_key
    burst: { type: per_key, tokens: 2000, window_s: 60 }
  enterprise:
    enforcement: per_org
    burst: { type: shared_org_pool, tokens: 100000, window_s: 60 }
```

Routing logic:
1) if org.bound_pool -> route to pool executor (enforcement = pool)
2) else if org.override -> use org enforcement
3) else use plan default
```

Jess: Looks good. We should also add a softcap grace window config so small spikes don't instantly throttle: `grace_ms` and `penalty_backoff` metrics.
Maya: Console UX: show current usage as three stacked bars: per-key, org-shared (if any), and plan-allocated. Hover shows which constraint fired most recently.
Arthur: For telemetry, ensure we emit events on enforcement decisions: `enforcement_evaluated` with fields `[quota_mode, limit, used, burst_applied]`. That helps evals + billing.
Ravi: Edge case: multi-key clients (one org using many API keys) — if we keep per-key as default for pro, admins may abuse by creating many keys. Need rate-of-key-creation quota or evaluate aggregate usage per org for heuristics.
Tom: Agree. Add `key_creation_rate_limit` at org level and a console flag for auto-grouping (suggest merging keys into org aggregate for billing).
Jess: For rollback/rollout: start by enforcing per-key for 90% of traffic, log decisions, then flip for orgs with Dedicated binding. Use canary and a console toggle.
Maya: Can we ship a small migration plan doc for CS so they can explain to customers? Short bullets: what changes, what UI they'll see, how to request org overrides.
Arthur: I'll draft the doc. Also will add a telemetry dashboard in Console under "Quota enforcement" to show fired constraints over time.
Ravi: One more: tests. Need unit tests for precedence matrix and e2e that simulates bursts across keys and org pool.
Maya: OK — action items: (1) Arthur draft CS doc + dashboard, (2) Eng implement enforcement_mode + labels, (3) DevEx add console UX mockups, (4) QA build e2e tests.
Jess: Adding to roadmap board. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Tom: I'll own the routing change.
Ravi: I'll add PR with config schema and tests.
QuotaBot: Note: created ticket Q-4821 for enforcement_mode feature.
Maya: Great — meeting if needed tomorrow. :calendar:
